findings.title: Distinguish an unreadable baseline before classifying IDs as new
findings.body: `check` always passes `baselineIDs(baselineLevels(tree))` here, but `baselineLevels` returns an empty map when HEAD cannot be listed/read and drops a summary's IDs when its baseline cannot parse. Consequently, a permanent ID with a corrected citation (for example `RFC9999-2-1` citing §2.1) is reported as a new misanchored ID in a source export without Git or after a baseline-read failure. This contradicts the documented rule that unavailable baselines judge nothing and makes the newly supported correction fail solely because its allocation history is unavailable. Preserve baseline-read status (including unreadable summary scope), skip the allocation comparison where it is unknown, and cover that path through `Check` while retaining checks for a known-empty baseline.

explanation: The parser-to-allocation split preserves structural validation and routes new-ID refusals through Check, but unavailable or unparsable HEAD baselines are mistaken for known absence, incorrectly rejecting permanent IDs whose citations were corrected. Coverage and proof remain independently derived; the deleted mismatch assertions have real-entry-point replacements. This is a scoped source review only: Main owns validation and the concurrently revised positive-test oracle.
